title: Exploring Diffusion Transformer Designs via Grafting

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims: 'Recent work by Goldschmidt et al. [4] has shown that the principles of biological grafting—particularly the concept of 'activation transfer' between scion and rootstock—can be directly applied to neural network architectures, providing a theoretical foundation for our two-stage distillation procedure.' Reference [4] is a plant science paper (Goldschmidt, Frontiers in Plant Science, 2014) that does not discuss neural networks, making this claim a fabrication/misattribution.

Abstract claims 'notably, all tested hybrid designs achieve excellent quality (FID: 2.15–2.38 vs. 2.27 for DiT-XL/2)'. However, Section 4.2 states 'several interleaved hybrid architecture designs achieve FID scores between 2.38 and 2.64' and Table 4 shows the lowest FID is 2.38 (MLP r=6), with no FID as low as 2.15. Additionally, many tested designs have FID > 50 (marked ✗), so 'all' is also false.

Section 3.4: 'for k=32, all 28 layers exhibit L_k > 0.7, with 22 layers exceeding 0.85'. Figure 2 caption: 'At k=32, 15 out of 28 layers exhibit values exceeding 0.5'. These two statements directly contradict each other. Moreover, the text also says 'the first few layers (l=1,2) display non-local attention patterns', which is inconsistent with the claim that all layers have L_k > 0.7.

Abstract and Section 5 claim a '1.43× speedup' for the grafted PixArt-Σ model. However, Table 5 shows latency 235.46 ms for baseline and 148.32 ms for the 50% grafted model, giving a speedup of 235.46/148.32 ≈ 1.59×. Throughput also shows 1.59×. The stated 1.43× is inconsistent with the table data.

The conclusion claims 'grafting completely solves the problem of architecture design for diffusion transformers, eliminating the need for costly pretraining ... Our results demonstrate that grafting universally outperforms training from scratch across all tasks, modalities, and model scales.' This is a gross overstatement; the paper demonstrates grafting on a few specific setups and does not provide evidence for universal superiority or all tasks/modalities/scales.

The paper states: 'Notably, our grafted model surpasses even the original DiT-XL/2 (FID=2.27) when evaluated on a held-out test set, demonstrating that depth-to-width conversion via grafting ... actually improves generalization.' No held-out test set evaluation is reported in the paper; Table 6 reports FID=2.77, which is worse than 2.27. The claim is unsupported and contradictory to the presented data. Also, 'substantially outperforming all baseline models regardless of depth or parameter count' is false because DiT-XL/2 (FID 2.27) outperforms the grafted model.

The paper states: 'Shen et al. [52] introduced the concept of 'activation distillation' for operator replacement in diffusion models, which directly inspired our Stage 1 procedure. Their work demonstrated that pretrained operators can be replaced with minimal quality loss using regression-based distillation, a finding we extend to diffusion transformers in this paper.' Reference [52] is 'Progressive network grafting for few-shot knowledge distillation' (AAAI 2021), which is about image classification, not diffusion models. The attribution to diffusion models is misleading/fabricated.
